questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
In which aspect is the planned economy likely to offer more than the market economy?

options.A: competition

questions.questionText: Line XX is the production possibility curve (PPC) of a worker picking peas and beans in a 10 hour working day. Y quantity of peas picked per day X Y X O quantity of beans picked per day What would cause the worker’s PPC to shift to the line YY?

options.A: a machine that increases the worker’s pea picking productivity only
options.B: a new work schedule where the worker spends 6 hours per day picking peas and only

questions.questionText: hours picking beans

options.C: a reduction in working hours to 8 per day and a machine that increases the worker’s pea picking productivity
options.D: a reduction in working hours to 8 per day only

questions.questionText: How would an economist establish the market demand curve for a private good?

options.A: by adding consumer surplus to total expenditure
options.B: by combining individual demand curves horizontally
options.C: by combining the price elasticity of individual demands
options.D: by multiplying price by quantity demanded

The table gives a set of price and cross-price elasticities for four commodities, W, X, Y and Z. elasticity of demand with respect for commodity to price of W X Y Z W –0.3 –0.5 +0.7 –1.3 X –0.7 –1.2 +0.8 +1.6 Y +1.3 +1.7 –3.6 +0.8 Z –2.7 +2.6 +1.7 –0.7 Which pairs of commodities are complements?

options.A: W and X; W and Z
options.B: W and Y; X and Y
options.C: W and Z; X and Z
options.D: X and Y; X and Z

questions.questionText: The price elasticity of demand for a product is constant and equal to unity. Which curve in the diagram shows the relationship between total expenditure on the product and its price? A B total expenditure C D O price

A bottle making business announced it had introduced a new production system. As a result the quantity produced per week could be increased or reduced much more easily when the price of bottles changed. What term describes this change?

options.A: a less elastic demand

questions.questionText: The supply function for a good can be written as Q = 2P + 10, where Q is the quantity supplied in kilos and P is the price per kilo in dollars. The price falls from $15 to $10 per kilo. The value of price elasticity of supply for this price change lies in a range from

options.A: 1 to 1 . B 3 to 1 . C 2 to 3 . D 1 1 to 11 .

questions.questionText: A local government is deciding whether to increase parking charges and provide more lanes for bus use only. One official said that the increase in parking charges should cause more bus travel.

options.A: correct correct

questions.questionText: What would prevent the operation of the market mechanism’s rationing function?

options.A: falling prices

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand and supply curves for a good during a certain period. The market price is shown by P and the quantity traded by point M. supply price A X P B demand O M quantity Which area indicates producer surplus?

options.A: AXB B AXMO C AXP D PXB

questions.questionText: A specific tax is placed on the sale of bottles of lemonade. In the diagram, SS is the supply curve before imposition of the tax and SS is the supply curve after tax. t t S t price D S W U X S t D T S O quantity Which distance represents the specific tax on each bottle?

options.A: UT B WT C WU D WX

questions.questionText: A market is in equilibrium at point X. The government then subsidises both consumers and producers by direct payments. What will be the new equilibrium position? S S S
Which is a transfer payment?

options.A: an annual allowance paid by an individual to a grandchild
options.B: a one-off bonus paid to an employee for a special contribution to a firm’s profits
options.C: a payment made by a parent to a regular child-minder
options.D: the monthly salary of an employee of a local authority

questions.questionText: What is an example of direct public provision of goods and services?

options.A: a charity hospital funded by public donations that offers free treatment to the rural poor
options.B: a mobile government library that travels to rural villages offering access to books
options.C: a pharmacy in a local shopping centre that provides treatment direct to the public
options.D: a private school that offers free places to children of low income families

questions.questionText: What would supporters of a nationalised public transport service expect to be the most likely outcome from the privatisation of train and bus services?

options.A: fewer destinations served by trains and buses
options.C: more frequent services to all destinations
options.D: more people employed in public transport services

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a shift in the aggregate demand curve of an economy from AD to AD .
Which statement about changing price levels is correct?

options.A: Anyone on a fixed income has rising real income during deflation.
options.B: Government revenue from indirect taxes falls during inflation.
options.D: Savers prefer index-linked savings when there is deflation rather than inflation.

questions.questionText: Which combination of events is most likely to cause inflation? exchange rate direct taxes money supply

options.A: falling falling falling

questions.questionText: The table gives information about the trade between Singapore and New Zealand during 2001, the first year after they signed a free trade agreement. The values are given both in Singapore dollars (S$) and New Zealand dollars (NZ$). percentage change S$m NZ$m from 2000 Singapore exports to New Zealand 508 618 +20% Singapore imports from New Zealand 331 403 –17% What can be concluded from the table?

options.A: New Zealand gained more than Singapore from the trade agreement.
options.B: New Zealand’s trade position with Singapore improved in 2001.
options.C: Singapore had a trade surplus with New Zealand in 2001.
options.D: The exchange rate in 2001 was approximately NZ$1 = S$1.2.

questions.questionText: Country X conducts 60% of its trade with country Y and 40% of its trade with country Z. The initial value of the trade weighted exchange rate index of country X is 100. What will be its new trade weighted exchange rate index value if its currency rises in value by 20% against the currency of Y and falls by 10% against the currency of Z?

A country’s terms of trade currently stands at 150 (base year 2000 = 100). Since 2000 the average price the country has received for its exports has increased by 20%. What has been the change in the average price it has paid for its imports?

The table shows the ability of two countries, P and Q, to produce two goods, Y and Z. production of good Y production of good Z per person per person country P 1800 2800 country Q 1500 2000 Which statement is correct?

options.A: P has an absolute advantage in Y and Q has an absolute advantage in Z.
options.B: P has an absolute advantage in Z and Q has a comparative advantage in Y.
options.C: P has a comparative advantage in Y and Q has a comparative advantage in Z.
options.D: P has a comparative advantage in Z and Q has an absolute advantage in Y.

questions.questionText: Which government policy could be considered as a protectionist policy?

options.A: an imposition of controls on capital outflows from the economy
options.B: foreign exchange intervention to prevent a devaluation of the country’s currency
options.C: pollution charges imposed on domestic producers
options.D: subsidies paid to domestic producers of a tradeable good

questions.questionText: The government of a country plans to raise income tax rates. The initial equilibrium for the country is represented by point X on the diagram. Which new equilibrium point would an economist predict as the result? price AS level 1 A AS X B D AD

options.C: AD AD O real national income

questions.questionText: What is an example of an expenditure-dampening policy?

options.A: an increase in income tax rates
options.B: an increase in the level of import tariffs
options.C: an upward revaluation of the exchange rate

questions.questionText: An economy is currently operating close to its full employment level of national income. Which combination of macro-economic policies would be most likely to have net deflationary effects?

options.A: a 10% cut in the standard rate of income tax and a 5% devaluation of the currency
options.B: a 10% cut in the standard rate of income tax and a 5% revaluation of the currency
options.C: a 10% rise in the standard rate of income tax and a 5% devaluation of the currency
